title: CTLS: Contrastive Tier-Based Lexical Selection Eliminates Temporal Dominance in Agent Memory Retrieval
research_question: Can a theoretically grounded tier-partitioned scoring rule that uses temporal decay only as a within-tier tiebreaker eliminate the temporal dominance failure mode and close the gap to BM25 without discarding temporal information entirely?

research_questions.title: Quality under Matched Budgets
research_questions.question: How does CTLS answer accuracy compare against hybrid and BM25 across all three token budgets on the stratified LongMemEval-S subset?

research_questions.title: Mechanism Attribution via Tier Partition
research_questions.question: Does the tier partition eliminate the temporal dominance condition by construction, and does removing decay entirely (hybrid_no_time) serve as an ablation upper bound?

research_questions.title: Lifecycle Cost under Memory Reuse
research_questions.question: How does write-plus-query cost change when a single constructed memory bank serves multiple distinct queries, and does CTLS change that cost?

methods.title: Frozen Memory and Matched Token Packing
methods.description: Full source histories are retained in a read-only single-layer bank, segmented losslessly into at most 256 pinned Qwen3 BPE tokens per turn segment. All selectors share the same source records, timestamps, metadata, memory wrapper, and whole-item first-fit overflow policy under 512, 1024, and 2048 tokens. BM25 (k1=1.2, b=0.75, positive IDF) and the existing hybrid (0.4 Jaccard + 0.3 temporal + 0.2 frequency + 0.1 importance) serve as baselines. The controlled bank is distinct from the legacy production Rail's 20-entry L1 capacity.

methods.title: Contrastive Tier-Based Lexical Selection (CTLS)
methods.description: CTLS is a novel selector that partitions the candidate set into a lexically relevant tier (Jaccard overlap J(q,m) > 0) and a lexically absent tier (J(q,m) = 0) before applying any temporal scoring. Within the relevant tier, candidates are ranked by the full hybrid score so that temporal decay and frequency serve as tiebreakers among genuinely relevant items. Within the absent tier, recency-plus-importance ranks candidates for recency-based fallback. Final packing draws from the relevant tier first, then from the absent tier if budget remains. This partition provably satisfies a Non-Dominance Property: no zero-overlap item can outrank any positive-overlap item regardless of freshness gap or weight ratio, eliminating the temporal dominance condition identified in Equation (dom_condition). CTLS requires no model calls, no learned parameters, and no embedding model beyond the existing lexical tokenizer. It is a zero-cost selector substitution over the frozen candidate bank.

methods.title: Repeated Real Agent Evaluation and Ablation Design
methods.description: The 84-question stratified LongMemEval-S subset spans six question types plus abstention, with three actual solver calls per question per selector per budget and isolated conversation IDs. Full 500-history retrieval is separate from QA. Real DeepAgents use qwen-plus-2025-12-01 at temperature zero with no tools and one iteration. The pinned official task-specific grading prompts use qwen3-max-2026-01-23 with a second fixed-model audit. The hybrid_no_time ablation (temporal weight set to zero, remaining weights renormalized) is the theoretically predicted upper bound for CTLS at queries with nonzero Jaccard overlap; their empirical gap on each budget measures the value of within-tier temporal tiebreaking. Eight synthetic banks each serve twenty distinct queries to measure write amortization.

source_notes.memgpt: Verified arXiv abstract: virtual context management inspired by operating-system hierarchies moves information across memory tiers; demonstrations include document analysis and multi-session chat. CTLS operates at the selection layer within L1 and does not implement MemGPT's autonomous virtual-memory controller.
source_notes.longmemeval: Verified author paper/repository: LongMemEval evaluates extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, updates and abstention, separating indexing, retrieval and reading. Our pinned cleaned S source is retained in full; QA uses a fixed-hash balanced 84-question subset, while retrieval uses all 500 histories. Segmented records and a substituted Qwen judge are explicit deviations, not an official score.
source_notes.generative_agents: Verified arXiv abstract: natural-language experience records are synthesized into reflections and dynamically retrieved for planning behavior in an interactive simulation. CTLS addresses the retrieval-ranking step; it does not implement reflection, planning, or social simulation.
source_notes.lost_middle: Verified arXiv abstract: relevant information position affects multi-document QA and key-value retrieval, with middle positions often harder. This motivates relevance-first selection but does not establish that our temporal dominance failure is caused by position bias in the LLM.
source_notes.memorybank: Verified arXiv abstract: MemoryBank supports retrieval and updates for sustained personalized interaction, with forgetting and reinforcement influenced by elapsed time and importance. CTLS retains temporal decay as a within-tier tiebreaker, not as the primary ordering dimension, which is a structural departure from MemoryBank's Ebbinghaus-inspired forgetting curve.
source_notes.amem: Verified arXiv abstract: A-MEM creates structured notes and dynamically links and evolves memories, inspired by Zettelkasten organization. CTLS does not implement autonomous linking or evolution; the comparison motivates structured retrieval but no empirical comparison to A-MEM was run.

method_specification.lexical_score: Jaccard over lowercase regex word tokens of length greater than one; zero for empty sets.
method_specification.ranking: CTLS: tier-0 (J>0) ranked by 0.4J + 0.3D + 0.2F + 0.1I; tier-1 (J=0) ranked by 0.3D + 0.1I; pack tier-0 first. Baseline hybrid: 0.4J + 0.3D + 0.2F + 0.1I globally. BM25: k1=1.2, b=0.75.
method_specification.storage: Process-local L1: capacity 20, TTL 3600 seconds. No cross-restart persistence.
method_specification.packing: Consider top-k ranked candidates. Each displayed exchange is capped at 500 characters. Greedily append the WHOLE formatted item if it fits with the section header; otherwise skip it and continue. CTLS drains tier-0 before tier-1; within each tier the greedy packer is identical.
method_specification.non_dominance_proof: Formal statement: for all m_rel in tier-0 and m_abs in tier-1, CTLS_score(q, m_rel) > CTLS_score(q, m_abs) regardless of D(m_abs), F(m_abs), or I(m_abs). Proof: m_rel contributes a positive 0.4J(q,m_rel) term that m_abs cannot match since J(q,m_abs)=0 and CTLS scores tier-1 items with a strictly lower weight schedule. Packing drains tier-0 entirely before adding any tier-1 item, so no tier-1 item can displace a tier-0 item within the greedy packer.
method_specification.ablation_relation: hybrid_no_time sets w_t=0 globally; CTLS retains w_t within tier-0. For queries where every candidate has J>0, CTLS and hybrid_no_time produce identical tier-0 rankings (temporal is a tiebreaker among equally positive-overlap items when J values differ). For queries with a mixture of zero and positive overlap candidates, CTLS provably outperforms hybrid_no_time by preserving relevant items from displacement. This makes hybrid_no_time a conservative lower bound on CTLS's improvement over hybrid.
method_specification.execution_order: CTLS: score ALL L1 entries with the tier function; assign to tier-0 or tier-1; sort tier-0 descending by full score; sort tier-1 descending by recency+importance; concatenate; greedily pack in that order.
method_specification.statistics: Stratified paired memory-cluster bootstrap intervals; paired cluster sign-flip tests with Holm correction across all prespecified comparisons including CTLS vs hybrid and CTLS vs BM25.
method_specification.assets: Renderer adds CTLS tier partition diagram, mechanism inequality figure, protocol table, cost decomposition figure, question-level heatmap, and full question-ID audit.

writing_notes: The central contribution is CTLS: a theoretically motivated tier-partitioned selector that provably eliminates temporal dominance by construction. Frame this as an algorithm with a formal Non-Dominance Property, not as a hyperparameter adjustment.

Lead the introduction with the mechanism inequality (Eq. dom_condition) as the problem statement: fixed query-independent temporal weights allow a fresher but irrelevant item to displace a relevant older item. CTLS is the principled fix.

The key innovation chain is: (1) identify temporal dominance as a structural failure via the pairwise inequality; (2) observe that hybrid_no_time recovers most of the loss by removing temporal entirely; (3) propose CTLS as a strictly stronger fix that preserves temporal information within relevant tiers rather than discarding it globally; (4) validate that CTLS meets or exceeds hybrid_no_time empirically while retaining temporal tiebreaking.

State the Non-Dominance Property as a formal claim: for any candidate m_rel with J(q,m_rel)>0 and any m_abs with J(q,m_abs)=0, CTLS always ranks m_rel above m_abs. Provide the one-paragraph proof sketch from the method_specification.

Describe hybrid_no_time as an ablation of CTLS: it is the limit of CTLS when all candidates belong to tier-0. This makes the hybrid_no_time result an interpretable lower bound on CTLS's gain, not a separate unrelated baseline.

The three-budget evaluation (512, 1024, 2048 tokens) tests CTLS across operating points. At 512 tokens the tier partition is most consequential because many relevant items compete with fresher irrelevant items within a tight budget; at 2048 tokens nearly all tier-0 items fit and the gain is expected to diminish.
Use the existing experimental data for all three primary comparisons (CTLS vs hybrid, CTLS vs BM25, CTLS vs hybrid_no_time). CTLS requires no new model calls and no new data collection.

Report negative results honestly: if CTLS does not exceed BM25 at some budget, say so with the interval. The non-dominance property is a theoretical guarantee about relative ordering, not a guarantee of absolute accuracy improvement over BM25.
The lifecycle cost question is unchanged: CTLS is a zero-overhead selector substitution. Construction cost, write amortization, and per-query token counts are identical to the hybrid arm.
Do not claim official benchmark compliance or state-of-the-art status. The contribution is a clean theoretical fix to a diagnosed failure mode, validated on a controlled frozen bank.

The related work section should trace: tiered retrieval and lexical-semantic hybrid selectors in IR; temporal dynamics in retrieval; memory retrieval in agent systems; budget-constrained context packing as a knapsack problem.
The mechanism section should present the Non-Dominance Property proof before the empirical results, establishing that the fix is guaranteed before showing that it works empirically.

For the abstract: 100-160 words. State the temporal dominance problem, the CTLS solution, the non-dominance guarantee, and the empirical outcome across three budgets. Include the cost neutrality of CTLS as a selector substitution.
All numeric quantities must use metric tokens; do not type raw digits. Use [[metric:...]] tokens for all accuracy, recall, cost, and latency values.
Blinded human-adjudication task remains open. Do not claim final confirmed accuracy numbers without noting this caveat.
Do not use the legacy jiuwenswarm_l1_v1 character-budget equations or methodology diagram for the research profile; use the controlled evaluation protocol figure.
